approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples parents from score quantiles, combines connected fragments and applies local edits, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on every earlier accepted score represents molecules by counts of local environments and uses generalized Tanimoto covariance to predict the pool. Independent correlated posterior draws currently choose each batch member, removing its identity before the next draw. Real accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Remove sampled uncertainty from the choice rule: submit the molecules with the highest posterior means, using pool order to break exact ties. Keep the learned model and the original draws, with those draws serving only as passive comparisons. Earlier siblings coordinated pending uncertainty or optimized a predicted batch maximum; both retained uncertainty in their decisions and neither improved the final mean score. This is the first supplied sibling to test mean-only allocation on the current Parent. It asks whether concentrating evaluations on predicted quality helps, while measuring the loss of uncertainty exposure and molecular-core coverage that the Parent-pool replay predicts.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 completes all supplied replicas with macro mean 0.574343936523512 and population SD 0.012316775530180069. Its count-based posterior is informative on the selected stream: chronological prediction MSE is 0.0112691820515 versus the same-fit archive-mean baseline 0.0425042191038, and mean within-batch rank correlation is about 0.550. However, only 624 of 4350 evaluated offspring strictly beat their best generating parent, and nominal 95 percent latent intervals cover 76.9 percent of the scored emissions. The one targeted behavior is that the allocation rule spends evaluations on sampled excursions away from the best predicted means, without isolated evidence that those excursions improve final solutions. Poor coverage and weak parent-beating yield do not themselves establish that exploration is harmful. A passive reconstruction of all 435 actual Parent pools, earlier accepted archives and recorded normal arrays with RDKit 2023.09.6 reproduces means and function draws within 1.17e-13. The Parent differs from the unique posterior-mean maximizer on its actual available mask at 3760 of 4350 positions; none of these disagreements is a tied mean maximum. Selecting the top ten means on those identical pools changes 4064 ordered positions and 433 batch sets, retaining 1732 actual set memberships. The median full-pool mean rank of an actual Parent emission is 16, and the 95th percentile is 115. Passive mean-only allocation raises the mean selected prediction from 0.4081113 to 0.4391780 and lowers mean original predictive SD from 0.0427635 to 0.0294660. It also raises mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation from 0.0489841 to 0.0713144 and reduces mean nonempty Murcko-core coverage from 6.9816 to 5.2391. These are decision and model-statistic counterfactuals with no assigned alternate oracle scores; they expose a concrete exploitation-versus-coverage tradeoff. The supplied sibling n-521f362b3777 correctly conditions later draws on pending means but has paired macro delta -0.00184421461498; n-9c0f6fa601f8 correctly maximizes a shared-panel batch-maximum objective but has delta -0.000364602244307. Both increase local parent-beating and incumbent-update counts without reaching the supplied final-score minimum. Neither removes sampled uncertainty from successful allocation. The older selector observation n-fc2c108a5253 and Curate cluster c-1e7b33da25 explicitly leave its marginal score contribution unresolved. The present probe addresses that specific unresolved contribution on the inherited count-posterior Parent.
hypothesis: Select each successful batch by stable descending posterior mean on the existing fresh pool, removing sampled uncertainty from the identity-allocation rule while retaining the learned count-based posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-only selection executed, narrowed chemical coverage, and reduced final macro score by 0.0404
finding_summary.insights:
This removal experiment supplies negative utility evidence for treating the sampled excursions as wasted evaluations. The learned mean remains informative against its own archive-mean baseline, but concentrating on its highest predictions produced more local improvements along a search that ended lower. Parent-beating yield and lower selected-stream prediction error therefore remain poor substitutes for final search quality. The model itself was frozen: lower SD exposure and lower error describe the selected molecules and their subsequent feedback, not improved uncertainty calibration.

Lost breadth is a plausible explanation to investigate. The chemistry assessment found fewer distinct cores in 14 of 15 paired streams, consistent with the matched-pool coverage loss. It also found persistent unusual bonds, burdensome decorations and unspecified stereochemistry, so more selective allocation did not establish better chemical feasibility. The result narrows the next question to which exploratory choices or independent molecular families help preserve useful search paths. It does not identify a particular discarded molecule as the missing winner: alternate choices have no counterfactual oracle outcomes, and the downstream histories differ. Transfer beyond this Parent and supplied panel remains open.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,350 successful choices followed the stable highest-mean order, with zero violations. On the same 435 Child pools, the inherited sampled rule would have selected a different set in every batch. Mean-only selection raised average predicted quality from 0.357917 to 0.390251 and reduced original prediction SD from 0.038134 to 0.020556. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation rose from 0.054704 to 0.064071, count-fingerprint similarity rose from 0.5810 to 0.8211, and distinct nonempty chemical cores fell from 6.503 to 4.437 per ten molecules. These are comparisons on identical pools and model distributions.

The completed search scored worse. Three-seed final macro mean fell from 0.574344 to 0.533937, a paired change of -0.040407 against the required +0.002. All three macro replicas declined. Task mean changes were -0.104061 for sitagliptin_mpo, -0.043769 for drd2_docking, -0.036782 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.018368 for deco_hop, and +0.000944 for median_2. This occurred despite strict parent-beating offspring increasing from 624 to 707 out of 4,350 and batches improving the incumbent increasing from 182 to 197. Mean accepted batch-best fell from 0.487313 to 0.437676. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.004397, while within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.316. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.24% of Child scores, versus 76.92% for the Parent. All batches were complete and accepted, with no numerical fallback.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families narrow around ordinary drug-like cores, but unusual bonds, oversized decorations and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character:
Read all supplied trajectories for node n-852bc7be4d7c and Parent n-559d25e9c9c7: each covers the five tasks at seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 scored rows per task, including 870 optimizer proposals. No task lacks trajectories. The digest pools seeds: its leading indole, amine-rich and polycyclic-dione examples come from seed 2, and its leading heavily decorated and fluorinated diones come from seed 1. The other seed families are included below from their full trajectories. Scores quoted here are recorded values; displayed endpoint decimals are rounded.

The output consists of connected, ring-rich molecules carrying aromatic or heteroaromatic cores, amide/lactam carbonyls, ethers, variable nitrogen functionality and frequent halogens. These are not predominantly tiny fragments. The digest ring-closure rate is 1.0 for every task; its aromatic-atom presence rate is 1.0 except 0.9989 for the fluorinated-dione task. These are molecule-presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. All task counters show zero explicit charge and zero stereocentre markers.

Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 inspection of the supplied optimizer rows finds all 4350 recorded Child optimizer proposals parse, while 1768 have at least one graph-perceived unassigned chiral centre and none has an assigned one. Parsing does not establish stability, a realizable stereoisomer or a synthesis. Some indole carboxamides have recognizable medicinal chemistry; other leading families contain highly decorated halogenated acetals, peroxide/polysulfide tethers, sulfur doubly bonded to two carbons, or complicated ring closures. The weak drug-likeness judgement reflects these recurring liabilities and large structures, not an absence of medicinal-chemistry motifs.

Distinct nonempty atom-and-bond Murcko core counts fall in 14 of 15 paired streams; the exception rises from 41 to 47. This supports narrow within-stream coverage, although the pooled panel contains several distinct families and genuine ring edits. Core counts retain heteroatom and bond-order changes and are not counts of independent synthetic scaffold families. The passive audit, including trajectory hashes, descriptor definitions and per-seed high/low summaries, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-10-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. No oracle, biological validation or synthesis-route calculation was performed.

per_task.generated_character: Compact indole-like aromatic families dominate all seeds. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts are 25, 25 and 24 in seed order; each has a median of three aromatic rings. The digest leader is a neutral indole carboxamide linked to a pyridyl ring, with methyl/vinyl and methoxy or vinyl-ether substituents: 24 heavy atoms, molecular weight 319.36 Da and three aromatic rings. Its secondary amide and indole NH provide donors, with carbonyl/ether/pyridyl acceptor sites. Full trajectories show seed 0 also favouring N-hydroxy hydrazide-like links, and seed 1 favouring bromomethylated N-amino/imine variants. Thus the clean pyridyl amide leader does not represent all emitted chemistry. The ordinary amide family is plausibly approachable; the heteroatom-linker variants are less routine. Parent and Child retain similar typical size, but pooled distinct Murcko cores contract from 276 to 103.
liabilities: The leading vinyl ether and pendant alkenes introduce stability/reactivity questions; they are not themselves evidence that the molecules are unmakeable.

Acyl fluoride, bromomethyl, N-O/N-N and O-S-O variants broaden the graph vocabulary without demonstrated handling of their functional-group chemistry. The digest halogen-presence rate is 0.8632 even though its highest-scoring examples are halogen-free.
missing_features: Alternative compact heteroaromatic core architectures preserving the useful amide and donor/acceptor arrangement are poorly represented among leaders; existing pyridyl positional variation is present and should not be mistaken for a missing capability.

The cleaner pyridyl amide arrangement is not reproduced among the other seeds' leading families, which instead alter the polar link through hydrazide/imine chemistry. A tractable route to varying this arrangement without those link changes remains unshown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited initial trimethoxy, fluorophenyl indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The leading pyridyl, vinyl/ether variants reach 0.4330127018922193; pyridyl position and placement of the unsaturated substituents can change without changing this top value. A smaller dihalobenzene scores 2.2064040954992307e-13, an expanded heteroaromatic assembly with bromomethyl groups scores 1.389263800640293e-08, and an indole acyl fluoride scores 0.0012711582014672507. This supports a bounded-size, intact aromatic/polar arrangement rather than arbitrary aromatic content or growth. Late replacement of the ether with an O-S-O-containing tether gives 0.38171497280435657. These are multi-feature associations; the data do not establish an obligatory missing target group. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.457660 to 0.416350, 0.442313 to 0.388678, 0.448414 to 0.433013.

per_task.generated_character: Large, multiply substituted nitrogen heteroaromatic diones dominate. Median optimizer heavy-atom counts are 45, 46 and 45 across seeds, with corresponding median ring counts of seven, five and five. Seed 1 keeps an N-alkylated fused dione core and several aryl/azaaryl rings, then adds fluorinated/chlorinated alkyl groups, an imidate-like side chain and an O-C-O-C(Cl)-N-containing acetal/aminal-like tether. Its cited leader has 54 heavy atoms, five aromatic rings and molecular weight 811.09 Da; another near-top example has 63 heavy atoms and weighs 969.64 Da. Seed 0 instead develops a more cyclized azaaromatic assembly and long oxygen chains: 269 of its 290 optimizer molecules contain an O-O bond. Seed 2 retains the dione/azaaryl ester assembly and develops sulfur-containing tails, visible in the cited final molecules. These are coherent families but demanding synthetic proposals. Relative to Parent, the seed-0 median shrinks from 91 to 45 heavy atoms while seed 2 grows from 31 to 45; a single overall size-change description would be misleading.
liabilities: High molecular weight, many aromatic rings and flexible substituted tails create a substantial physical-property and synthesis burden. Chlorinated acetal/aminal-like centres and imidates require chemistry beyond ordinary alkyl decoration.

The passive audit finds O-O bonds in 325 and S-S bonds in 72 of this task's 870 Child proposals. Peroxide and polysulfide chains need stability and compatibility assessment; their scores provide none.
Stereogenic substituted side chains are left unspecified. The 63-heavy-atom cited analogue has five graph-perceived unassigned chiral centres.
missing_features: Compact, independently varied decorations that retain useful heteroaromatic and polar environments without accumulating long heteroatom chains are missing among the Child leaders. The stronger compact Parent example supports keeping this possibility open, without establishing a matched causal comparison.

The leaders do not demonstrate a route-plausible range of ether, amine and carbonyl substituents at similar size and attachment geometry; a few families account for extensive local decoration. Pooled nonempty Murcko cores fall from 415 in Parent to 105 in Child.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial ester/phenol dione scores 0.548381482770623. A compact bis-pyridyl dione scores 0.5385026737967915, and simple hydroxyl or partially dearomatized analogues remain around 0.5427-0.5447. More elaborate heteroaryl substitution and longer heteroatom/alkyl decorations accompany the 0.6014791881664947 leader. Added size alone is insufficient: the cited 63-heavy-atom analogue scores slightly less, 0.6011334766464725. Sulfur-rich late seed-2 products remain near 0.595, despite O-S-S-S-containing and related tethers. This gradient tolerates chemically questionable decoration; it does not validate it. The Parent seed-2 leader reached 0.616992140985949 with 30 heavy atoms, further showing that a much larger assembly is not demonstrably required. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.609280 to 0.593697, 0.619982 to 0.601479, 0.616992 to 0.595975.

per_task.generated_character: Halogenated aryl groups are combined with increasingly accessible amine functionality and partially saturated rings. Median heavy-atom counts are 32, 33 and 32 across seeds, with median aromatic-ring counts of two throughout. Seed 0 concentrates on a substituted cyclopentadiene joining aryl and amino-bearing sulfinamide chemistry; seed 1 develops an amine/amidine-rich fused and bridged polycycle. Seed 2, which supplies all digest leaders, joins two substituted aryl groups to a seven-membered diaza ring and an additional secondary amine. The first cited leader has 31 heavy atoms, three rings, molecular weight 467.05 Da, a phenol and an aniline, and sulfur doubly bonded to two terminal methylene carbons. That sulfur connectivity is graph-valid but far removed from the original sulfonamide chemistry. There is no shortage of amine centres in the successful products. Every Child optimizer molecule in this task has a graph-perceived unassigned chiral centre.
liabilities: Sulfur doubly bonded to two carbons occurs in 226 of 290 seed-2 proposals, including its leaders. RDKit acceptance is not evidence that this unusual sulfur functionality is stable or synthetically accessible.

The other seeds carry their own unresolved chemistry: densely fused amine/amidine rings, sulfenamide-like N-S connectivity or substituted cyclopentadiene systems. Their different chemistry should not be hidden behind the pooled best example.
All 870 proposals contain halogens and all 870 have unassigned graph-perceived chirality; size and binding scores alone do not settle chemical quality.
missing_features: Ordinary, tractable linkers that preserve the observed aryl-to-amine arrangement without the double-methylene sulfur centre are not demonstrated among the seed-2 leaders. The useful amine motif is already present; its chemical setting is the gap.

Defined stereoisomers and checked ring/side-chain geometry are absent despite the saturated, multiply substituted structures. Explicit charge states are also absent, so the visible neutral amines do not establish their protonation during scoring.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial acidic amide/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.01904115112334333; cited related early products score 0.009976648048984032-0.014368314381838294. They contain multiple carbonyl/acid groups and nitrogen tied into amide or sulfonamide environments. Higher products remove much of this acidic/carbonyl burden and expose amine-like nitrogen alongside aryl surfaces; the leading diaza-ring example reaches 0.9655637585918335. A primary-amine-containing analogue reaches 0.9588401522964047. The high-versus-low comparison in every seed supports this polar-functionality change, with reduced size also evident in the high-score groups. It cannot isolate the contribution of the unusual sulfur centre, predict protonation, or establish a binding mechanism. The full Parent trajectories reached their best values in amine-containing families without the Child's double-carbon sulfur motif. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.995949 to 0.945006, 0.996455 to 0.941817, 0.991289 to 0.965564.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized aryl/dione families undergo ring closure and partial saturation rather than extensive size growth. Median heavy-atom counts are 34, 33 and 35 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. Seed 0 develops fused oxygen-containing aryl systems and expanded dione rings; seed 1 stays more aromatic with ether/acetal bridges. Seed 2 produces the digest leaders: propyl- and ethoxy-substituted aryl groups, lactam carbonyls and a tertiary amine embedded in a fused/bridged polycycle. Its top cited structure has 35 heavy atoms, molecular weight 473.62 Da and five RDKit rings, of which two are aromatic; its perceived ring sizes include a four-membered ring and a ten-membered ring. Another near-top connectivity has five rings with smallest/largest perceived sizes five and eight. These are structurally varied ring systems, but their geometry and preparation remain unverified. The more aromatic seeds explain why the pooled median still has four aromatic rings.
liabilities: Small rings combined with larger bridged/fused cycles and unsaturation can impose substantial geometric and synthetic constraints. The recorded scores and ring perception do not prove that these conformations are realizable.

Late products also introduce N-O or N-S links within already complicated architectures. The score for the cited N-S-containing final example is 0.2262793367697775; this is not evidence for improved chemical tractability.
missing_features: Independent, geometrically credible arrangements of the aryl, ether, lactam and amine environments are underrepresented relative to repeated variants of a few ring frameworks. No exact missing target substructure follows from these scalar scores.

Specified relative and absolute stereochemistry is missing from the partially saturated polycycles. The leading structure has two graph-perceived unassigned centres; its near-top alternative has three.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/phenol fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, and cited early fluoro/chloro/amino aryl variants score 0.15402959422966314-0.15625847779496568. Replacing these decorations with propyl/ethoxy groups, changing carbonyl-ring connectivity and adding partially saturated cyclic/amine environments accompanies the leader at 0.2386887674913355. A different bridged-ring topology scores 0.2380664345096624. Seed-2 high-score products have fewer aromatic rings than its early low-score products, so simply adding aromaticity is not the observed direction. Both aromatic and less aromatic solutions remain in the other streams, and the multi-feature edits do not identify one required ring closure. Pooled Parent-to-Child Murcko coverage decreases from 566 to 224, while endpoint changes are mixed. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.222706 to 0.232446, 0.243215 to 0.227970, 0.230352 to 0.238689.

per_task.generated_character: Compact fluorinated derivatives of the N-alkylated fused dione replace the bulky initial decoration. Median heavy-atom counts are 28, 28 and 25 across seeds. Seed 0 develops cyclopropene, imine/oxime-like and N-F variants. Seed 1, which supplies the best digest examples, joins the dione to a fluorinated aryl ring fused to an N/O-containing ring; substituents include fluoromethoxy or fluoroethoxy groups. Its leader has 29 heavy atoms, molecular weight 414.32 Da and four rings, three aromatic, with a ring NH and an N-C-O-containing saturated segment. A different equal-scoring leader has an N-O bond. Seed 2 instead uses fluorinated alkyl substitutions and a seven-membered unsaturated oxygen ring bearing an OH; its cited leader has 27 heavy atoms, molecular weight 383.33 Da and three rings, two aromatic. These are distinct seed-specific products despite the common dione core.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds, N-O connectivity, cyclopropene rings and cumulated double bonds appear in the full proposal stream. The digest cumulated-double-bond presence rate is 0.054 and its halogen-presence rate is 0.9023. These observations warrant structure-specific chemistry checks, not a claim that every member is unstable.

The fluorinated cyclic N/O products contain unspecified stereogenic carbons. Carbon-bound fluorine in an ordinary ether or alkyl group should be distinguished from direct N-fluorination; the scalar scores do not validate either synthetic route.
missing_features: Controlled alternatives placing comparable carbon-bound fluorine and ordinary nitrogen/oxygen functions on different compact cores are poorly represented among leaders; both small fragments and oversized analogues miss the observed balance.

Defined stereochemistry for the fused N/O-ring family is absent. The equal best values for differing N-C-O versus N-O connectivity also leave the preferred polar geometry unresolved; a task-specific pharmacophore cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial ester/phenol dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. A larger cited aryl-extended ester analogue scores 2.861477157288716e-20, while a fluorobiphenyl fragment scores 1.5914126699678847e-18. The seed-1 N/O-ring leaders reach 0.5102212569858039 and the seed-2 fluorinated oxygen-ring example reaches 0.49929611529456036. The visible gradient therefore favours a bounded-size, fluorinated nitrogen/oxygen-containing assembly; neither fluorination alone nor growth suffices. Seed-1 N-C-O and N-O ring arrangements can share the same best score, so the data do not establish that an N-O bond is required. Late dione/fluoroalkyl edits range widely, including the cumulated-double-bond example at 0.37521555493964914 and an N-F/N-O-containing aryl product at 0.2227500990669383. Their multiple simultaneous changes preclude assigning these differences to one bond. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.651021 to 0.418851, 0.487006 to 0.510221, 0.602525 to 0.499296.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Distinct nonempty atom-and-bond Murcko core counts fall in 14 of 15 paired streams. The compact indole family contracts from 276 to 103 pooled cores and the heavily decorated dione family from 415 to 105. Several best-molecule excerpts contain positional or peripheral variants of one seed-specific framework. These are observed output restrictions, not proof that the generator is absolutely incapable of another scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted search does not sustain a broad range of chemical cores around productive local motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Create and retain independent core arrangements that preserve observed useful polar groups, approximate size and attachment relationships. Let accepted scalar feedback distinguish these alternatives. Further peripheral substitution alone does not demonstrate this missing breadth.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every recorded Child optimizer molecule parses, yet the leading amine-rich family contains sulfur doubly bonded to two carbons, present in 226 proposals. The decorated dione family contains O-O bonds in 325 proposals and S-S bonds in 72; its cited finals include extended sulfur/oxygen tethers. The fluorinated dione leaders include equal-scoring N-C-O and N-O ring alternatives, so unusual bonding is not uniformly required by the visible high scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Graph validity does not reliably preserve conventional bonding or manageable functional-group chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically interpretable alternatives for changing heteroatom functionality while preserving useful connections. Assess unusual sulfur valence, long heteroatom chains and direct nitrogen-halogen edits separately from ordinary ethers, amides and carbon-bound halogens. Neither parsing nor a high scalar score is a chemical-feasibility check.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading decorated dione has 54 heavy atoms and molecular weight 811.09 Da; a near-top analogue has 63 heavy atoms and weighs 969.64 Da while scoring slightly lower. The corresponding Parent stream also contains a stronger 30-heavy-atom endpoint. Other compact families lose score both on fragmentation and on excessive extension, so the panel does not support a universal smaller-is-better rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Decoration growth is not accompanied by reliable control of molecular size and synthetic burden.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support subtractive and size-preserving structural changes alongside growth, keeping useful functional-group relationships intact. Explore the empirically useful size region with simpler substituent chemistry rather than allowing chain length or repeated decoration to stand in for improved molecular design.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero. Passive graph inspection finds unassigned chiral centres in 1768 of 4350 Child optimizer rows and no assigned centres. The leading bridged dione combines small and large rings, while a near-top topology differs in ring sizes and has more unassigned centres; neither has a demonstrated realizable stereoisomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves stereochemistry and the geometry of newly created ring systems unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve, specify and validate stereochemical relationships when edits create saturated centres or ring junctions. Check geometric feasibility of constrained ring connectivity and distinguish graph-perceived possible chirality from realizable stereoisomers. The present scores do not establish a score gain from this capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring acidic amide/sulfonamide assemblies evolve into much higher-scoring aryl/amine families while size, rings and sulfur connectivity also change. Compact indole leaders preserve an amide but alter aryl nitrogen and unsaturation; fluorinated dione leaders alter ring topology and heteroatom bonding together. These contrasts reveal promising environments without identifying the causal contribution of one group.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful polar-functionality changes are often entangled with several unrelated chemical changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate local alternatives that vary donor/acceptor or amine connectivity while holding more of the surrounding framework and size fixed. Preserve explicit functional-group meanings and distinguish neutral amines from amide-bound nitrogen; derive any preference from observed feedback rather than assuming an objective-specific pharmacophore.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

method_references.title: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.
method_references.citation: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
Local atom/bond mutation, inner retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Direct formula-preserving same-six-member-aromatic-ring C/N positional exchange in the inherited per-site replacement menu, including its invariant gates and passive mutation-sequence receipts
Chemical sanitization, stable canonical/isomeric identity admission with graph-equivalent alias confirmation, novelty rejection and bounded graph-based retries for complete pools
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring
Accepted-only task-local Gaussian-process archive with full ordered accepted history, archive-mean centering, population-SD scaling and fixed observation noise
